findings.explanation: Terraform's built-in trim(string, cutset) function requires two arguments. `trim(var.role)` fails with "Not enough function arguments" during terraform validate/plan, unconditionally, for anyone consuming this module (confirmed with tofu validate). This looks like a typo for trimspace(), which takes a single string argument and does what the validation intends (reject blank/whitespace-only role values).
findings.remediation: Replace trim(var.role) with trimspace(var.role) in the validation condition.
findings.title: variable "role" validation calls trim() with a single argument, breaking terraform validate for every consumer

findings.explanation: members holds IAM member identifiers (e.g. "user:x@example.com"), which are always strings. list(any) defers type-checking to apply time and loses IDE/tooling autocomplete and static type errors that list(string) would provide for free.
findings.remediation: Change type to list(string). This narrows what callers can pass, so treat it as a minor-version change for a published module.
findings.title: variable "members" typed as list(any) instead of list(string)

findings.explanation: service is validated via contains(keys(var.service), "id") && contains(keys(var.service), "display_name") to simulate required fields. An object({ id = string, display_name = string }) type would enforce both required keys and their types structurally, making the custom validation redundant and giving callers a self-documenting schema instead of a bare map.
findings.remediation: Change type to object({ id = string, display_name = string }) and drop the now-redundant contains(keys(...)) validation (or keep it only if optional/extra keys should still be tolerated, in which case object(...) with optional() attributes is a closer fit).
findings.title: variable "service" typed as map(any) with a hand-rolled key-presence check instead of a typed object

findings.explanation: terraform.tf requires google = "7.30.0", but the committed .terraform.lock.hcl locks google to 3.59.0. A fresh `terraform init` / `tofu init` (no -upgrade) fails immediately with "Failed to resolve provider packages" (confirmed). Anyone cloning the repo and following the README's example cannot initialize it without already knowing to pass -upgrade.
findings.remediation: Regenerate the lock file with `tofu init -upgrade` (or `terraform init -upgrade`) and commit it so the constraint and lock agree. Note: running this under OpenTofu rewrites the lock file's registry host from registry.terraform.io to registry.opentofu.org — confirm that's acceptable for consumers who use plain Terraform before committing, or regenerate with the terraform CLI instead to keep the hashicorp registry host.
findings.title: example/examplea lock file pins google provider to a version that violates its own required_providers constraint
